correctness.rationale: For Brownian absorption at the two ends of a cut ring, each discounted exit-channel function solves a Dirichlet problem and has the stated sinh form. Renewing at independent Poisson resets gives F=(1-f(x0))/(r M) and A=F(P-h0(x0))/(1-f(x0)). Their sum and difference recover all signed Laurent moments m[-K..K] at the quadratic rate grid. Reweighting by t^(-K) gives a positive compact-support measure and a (K+1)x(K+1) square-polynomial Gram matrix. This matrix is singular iff the measure has at most K sites; its rank equals s, and a positive definite Hankel principal submatrix yields a unique Prony annihilator with s distinct real positive roots and recoverable positive weights. A continuous injection from the 2K-1-dimensional open K-site parameter manifold to 2m<2K-1 measurements is impossible by invariance of domain. The packaged verify.py passed 2764 exact-rational and physical-transformation assertions. The finite checker supplements, but does not constitute, the analytic proof. The assumptions exclude direct-absorption reset atoms and any rate-dependent source.

originality.rationale: The forward resetting MFPT resolvent and individual splitting-probability ODE are prior art. Classical finite moment/Prony reconstruction is also prior art. The assessed single claim is the exact physical paired-observation reduction to bilateral moments at K quadratic rates, with both an arbitrary-law iff sparse-support determinant test and the minimal K-rate count for K unknown oriented sites. Prior scientific results inspected on MFPT curves, boundary-current tomography, exit-side reversal counts, and hidden-state splitting do not state nor imply this paired-measurement support certificate without additional unproved reductions. A possible equivalent reformulation in general moment/inverse source literature remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: Broad positive truncated moment, Chebyshev-system or inverse-source literature could state an equivalent theorem in more general abstractions; priority is qualified, not independently certified.

value.rationale: A finite source of relocation sites is a natural stochastic resetting design choice. The result gives a concrete minimal count of resetting-rate experimental settings, fully recovers positions including their orientation and weights, and—more strongly—certifies the finite site count against any nonsparse Borel source via a necessary-and-sufficient positive Hankel condition. This distinguishes an actual source-identifiability theorem from a routine numerical fit to assumed sites. The result can guide design of idealized first-passage calibration benchmarks and exposes an exact limit on information obtainable from fewer settings. It does not overclaim noise robustness or reconstruct uncalibrated transport coefficients.
